claim: For l_p regression with p in (0,2], the algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup in the sample parameter m, which dominates runtime when m >> n (Corollary 11).
paper: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms (arXiv:2509.24757 / OpenReview TBSyYj4VV6)
method: Leverage-score sparsifier applied to l_p (IRLS, p=1.5) on full vs weighted sketch; m-scaling shows m>>n dominance; asymptotic symbolic.
reason: Sparsifier (1+/-eps) embedding holds (gram rel-err=0.108<=0.15); l_p optimum on sketch within 0.50 of full (ratio=0.184). m-scaling: full solve slope=1.94, sketch slope=0.45 -> m dominates when m>>n, consistent with quadratic speedup. Quantum/classical -> 0 as m->inf. EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: literal quantum construction (QRAM) NOT executed on CPU.

mutation.description: (M1) s<r/eps^2 breaks optimum-preservation; (M2) tighter eps needs more samples; (M3) quantum sqrt(m) required for speedup.
